scope: Focused review of the original case references and the linked vendor advisory. This is not an exhaustive search of all victim reports. Readable article text was reviewed; dynamically populated address tables were not independently extracted.

sources.title: The Coldcard wallet hack: $80M gone in 41 minutes
sources.support: Case-level reconstruction and transaction-pattern methodology. The author says victim addresses are withheld and address-role attributions are inferences.
sources.location: How this was reported; Evidence appendix; Legal disclaimer
sources.limitation: Does not establish independent victim or hardware control for any row in this 500-source cohort. A graph-derived population and a similarly sized published count do not create individual labels.

sources.title: Coldcard Security Advisory
sources.support: Describes vulnerable seed generation and qualifying device/firmware conditions. It also distinguishes seed compromise from remote takeover of a device.
sources.location: Opening advisory; Investigation and Firmware Status
sources.limitation: No reviewed evidence maps a cohort address to its owner, device, seed-generation firmware or compromise. The original publication date does not date every statement in the updated page.

sources.title: Predictable RNG Fallback and 32-Bit Reseed in COLDCARD Firmware
sources.support: Analyzes the firmware RNG construction and states that exporting an affected seed to another wallet does not repair that seed.
sources.location: Affected products; Impact due to seed export; Technical timeline
sources.limitation: Product-level findings cannot identify the device signing a particular historical transaction, nor independently verify that a cohort source was robbed. No seed/private-key recovery was attempted.

sources.source_type: Secondary incident reporting, used only for reference discovery and discrepancy review
sources.support: Links the vendor and technical reports and describes a roughly 500-wallet incident.
sources.limitation: The reported day and initial product assessment differ from parts of the pinned on-chain reconstruction/current vendor advisory. Do not rewrite the fixed 30 July cohort or infer per-address labels from aggregate reporting.

accepted_targets.compromised_source: Independent, dated evidence ties the exact address/outpoint/payment to funds taken without authorization. Transactional relationship alone is insufficient.
accepted_targets.hardware_seed_origin: Independent evidence ties the exact wallet/address to seed generation on the named device, with a relevant period and device/firmware details when vulnerability exposure is claimed.
accepted_targets.hardware_signing_at_event: A separate dated mapping supports hardware use for the relevant signing event. Seed origin or later export does not establish signing-device identity.

negative_control_requirement: Use a documented control-selection policy and evidence matching the exact target/time period. No report, no API error or no known hardware attribution is not a negative label.
evaluation_requirement: Define the label target before fitting; retain whole incident/entity groups and label-availability dates. The current single incident cannot supply an independent incident-level test.
decision: Keep compromise/hardware labels null. Do not fit the requested supervised detector from case-context reports alone.
